emergence.summary: A single-pathway disease caused by loss-of-function of either half of an obligate sterol-efflux pump. ABCG5 (sterolin-1) and ABCG8 (sterolin-2) form a heterodimeric ABC transporter that pumps absorbed plant sterols (sitosterol, campesterol) and excess cholesterol BACK out of the enterocyte into the gut lumen and out of the hepatocyte into bile -- the BRAKE that limits whole-body sterol retention. The two genes lie head-to-head at 2p21 sharing a bidirectional promoter, and biallelic LOF of EITHER subunit disables the shared pump, so dietary plant sterols and cholesterol are hyper-absorbed and under-excreted and ACCUMULATE -> the whole-body sterol load is driven UP, giving tendon/tuberous xanthomas, premature atherosclerosis and coronary disease, and stomatocytic haemolysis / macrothrombocytopenia from sterol-laden membranes. Read as a released BRAKE on sterol retention (ABCG5/ABCG8 efflux brakes it; LOF releases it -> sterols UP) -- the released-brake -> over-accumulation convention (tyrosinaemia / haemochromatosis / FCS) carried onto a NEW STEROL-ABSORPTION axis, and a TWO-CAUSAL-GENE read where both subunits perturb the same axis UP (the HCM convergence pattern; the deeper switch is picked as primary). The kit re-derives the targeted approved arm -- RESTRAIN the absorption axis with ezetimibe, which inhibits NPC1L1, the brush-border sterol-uptake transporter, cutting intestinal absorption of both plant sterols and cholesterol so the whole-body sterol load falls (ezetimibe is markedly effective in sitosterolaemia and is its mainstay). A low-plant-sterol diet and bile-acid sequestrants (cholestyramine, which interrupts enterohepatic sterol recycling) are adjuncts; statins are comparatively INEFFECTIVE here because the lesion is sterol ABSORPTION, not endogenous synthesis -- recorded as a downstream/poorly-matched NON-lever. This is the explicit CONTRAST to familial hypercholesterolaemia: FH is an LDL-cholesterol LEVEL axis (LDLR LOF / PCSK9 GOF, axis DOWN -> oppose PCSK9), whereas sitosterolaemia is a sterol-ABSORPTION axis (ABCG5/ABCG8 LOF, axis UP -> restrain absorption). The gamma reads are of the ABCG5 and ABCG8 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (e.g. ABCG8 p.Gly574Arg; ABCG5 truncations), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: whole-body sterol load (intestinal plant-sterol + cholesterol absorption / retention) -- a sterol-absorption axis; the absorption contrast to familial hypercholesterolaemia's LDL-cholesterol level axis

per_gene.note: ABCG5 encodes sterolin-1, one half of the ABCG5/ABCG8 heterodimeric sterol-efflux transporter that pumps plant sterols and excess cholesterol out of enterocytes (to the lumen) and hepatocytes (to bile) -- a BRAKE on whole-body sterol retention. Biallelic LOF disables the shared pump -> plant sterols and cholesterol are hyper-absorbed and under-excreted -> systemic sterol ACCUMULATION (axis UP). 2p21, head-to-head with ABCG8 on a shared bidirectional promoter (OMIM 605459). NCBI official symbol ABCG5. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/splice lesions are outside the promoter firewall.
per_gene.src: Berge 2000 Science 290:1771 (ABCG5/ABCG8 mutations cause sitosterolaemia); Yu 2002 J Clin Invest 110:671 (ABCG5/G8 are the sterol-efflux brake)

per_gene.note: ABCG8 encodes sterolin-2, the obligate partner subunit of the same sterol-efflux transporter; the functional pump is the ABCG5/ABCG8 heterodimer, so biallelic LOF of ABCG8 disables sterol efflux just as ABCG5 loss does -> the same released-brake -> sterol over-accumulation (axis UP). 2p21, head-to-head with ABCG5 (OMIM 605460). NCBI official symbol ABCG8. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding/splice lesions (e.g. the recurrent p.Gly574Arg allele) are outside the promoter firewall.
per_gene.src: Berge 2000 Science 290:1771 (ABCG5/ABCG8 in sitosterolaemia); Graf 2003 J Clin Invest 110:659 (ABCG5/G8 must heterodimerise to traffic and efflux sterol)

emergence.firewall: gamma reads promoter switch-threshold STRUCTURE only; perturbation DIRECTION is forced+cited; MAGNITUDE is [O] (runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable).

levers.push_direction: inhibit NPC1L1 to cut intestinal absorption of plant sterols and cholesterol -> lower the whole-body sterol load (axis DOWN toward healthy); bypasses the broken ABCG5/ABCG8 efflux pump
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of sterol-absorption reduction / plasma-sitosterol lowering not derived from sequence
levers.src: Salen 2004 Circulation 109:966 (ezetimibe lowers plasma sterols in sitosterolaemia); Altmann 2004 Science 303:1201 (NPC1L1 target); ezetimibe FDA 2002

levers.push_direction: interrupt enterohepatic sterol recycling with a bile-acid sequestrant so more sterol is excreted -> lower the whole-body sterol load (adjunct)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] degree of additional sterol excretion not derived from sequence; adjunct to absorption blockade

treatment_A_switch.firewall: levers are DIRECTION + cited agent CLASS; not dose/potency/efficacy/safety, not a recommendation to treat any individual.

falsifiers.claim: ABCG5 or ABCG8 LOF (released sterol-efflux brake) raises the whole-body sterol load (axis UP)
falsifiers.falsifier: an ABCG5 or ABCG8 LOF allele that LOWERED plasma plant-sterol / cholesterol absorption or RAISED biliary/luminal sterol efflux would refute the released-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: fractional cholesterol/sitosterol absorption and plasma plant-sterol (sitosterol, campesterol) levels by ABCG5/ABCG8 genotype

falsifiers.claim: restraining absorption (NPC1L1 inhibition) is the CORRECTIVE direction (lowers the sterol load)
falsifiers.falsifier: if inhibiting NPC1L1 with ezetimibe RAISED or failed to lower plasma plant sterols / sterol absorption in sitosterolaemia, the restrain-absorption lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: plasma sitosterol/campesterol and fractional sterol-absorption response to ezetimibe in sitosterolaemia
